properties.name: Every failure of a reflow2 tool met while working on reflow2 is captured on the record as a to-do — because it will surface in somebody else's design
properties.statement:
Set by Anthony on 2026-09-06, in his words: "I see occasional errors when you try to run one of the tools, like there was one for plan_epoch. If we are not at least capturing these failures as to-do items, then this is a big issue. We need to track where reflow2 fails, because if we're not addressing it here, then it'll come out when reflow2 is used in somebody else's design."

THE RULE: when a reflow2 tool refuses, errors, or has to be worked around during a session on reflow2 itself — a refusal whose remedy you had to find by hand, a warning on every write, a reply that did not say what you needed — the agent records it BEFORE moving on, as a dated TemporalFact (fact_type defect) on the capability or artifact the tool realizes, with the tool, the refusal text (ids masked), what was expected, and the workaround taken. Tier 1 of rule:every-failure-is-searched-and-every-cause-is-root-caused-before-it-is-written applies first: search the refusal text; a precedent gets a COUNTED recurrence on the existing record, not a second record. A refusal that is the loop working (a near-duplicate guard, a required field that the reply names correctly) is not a failure and is not recorded.

WHY: reflow2's own sessions are its first field. A refusal met here and worked around silently is the same refusal a user's agent will meet in their design, where nobody is watching for it and the workaround becomes a wrong edge or a lost round trip. Three were met in the session this rule was set in and none had been written down until he asked: plan_epoch's generic sequence refusal (a recurrence of a fact recorded the day before, on the sibling tool — fact:defect-add-epoch-requires-a-sequence-the-refusal-cannot-name-because-the-required-field-helper-is-generic), export_graph stamping a record from a replaced binary without a word (fact:defect-export-graph-stamps-confidently-while-the-server-reports-itself-stale), and create_node warning `undeclared: name` on every TemporalFact (fact:defect-temporal-fact-name-is-undeclared-while-49-facts-carry-one).

WHAT COMPLIANCE LEAVES BEHIND: one dated defect fact per distinct failure, or one counted recurrence; a session that met a refusal and left neither did not follow this rule. This is the same three-legs shape as the root-cause rules: the record is the second leg, and the detector that notices absence — the server counting its own refusals, which no agent has to remember — is owed and is recorded as an idea beside this rule.

ENFORCEMENT IS DELIBERATELY UNSTATED: whether a session that swallowed a refusal should fail anything is Anthony's to say.
